chunks: Al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā, from Ḥarīz, from Zurārah, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:
When you place the deceased in his niche-grave, then say: In the Name of Allah, and in the way of Allah, and upon the creed of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله.

And recite Āyat al-Kursī, and strike with your hand upon his right shoulder, then say: O so-and-so, say: I am satisfied with Allah as Lord, and with Islam as religion, and with Muḥammad as Messenger, and with ʿAlī as Imam; and the Imam of his time is to be named.

Then when the earth has been cast over him and his grave has been leveled, place your palm upon his grave near his head, spread your fingers apart, and press your palm upon it after it has been sprinkled with water.

key_terms.آيَةَ الْكُرْسِيِّ: the Quranic verse known for divine protection, recited here at burial
key_terms.إِمَامُ زَمَانِهِ: the Imam of the deceased person's own time
key_terms.بِعَلِيٍّ إِمَامًا: an affirmation of ʿAlī عليه السلام as Imam
key_terms.رَضِيتُ بِاللَّهِ رَبًّا: an affirmation of accepting Allah as Lord
key_terms.لَحْدِهِ: his grave niche within the burial place

ai.seo_question: What should be said and done when burying a deceased person according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith describes the recommended procedure of talqin for the deceased when placing him in the grave and after the burial is completed. It includes remembrance of Allah, recitation of Āyat al-Kursī, affirmation of core beliefs, and naming the Imam of the deceased's time, highlighting both burial etiquette and preparation for the afterlife.
